Response to the spec-degradation postmortem (#10). Root fix is doctrine, not checks: the spec's job is WHY / WHAT / WHERE; HOW is the plan's — and the kit's own text licensed the failure.

- **Principle #2 rewritten** — "specs carry design, not code" (which explicitly allowed referencing classes/methods/file paths) becomes **WHY/WHAT/WHERE — not HOW**, drawn as anchor-vs-prescription: existing code anchored at its stable surface (services, endpoints, topics, tables, config keys, DTO fields) plus a single interior name where the decision is genuinely about that artifact; invented interiors for not-yet-existing artifacts (a contract's *schema* is WHAT, its *carrier class* is HOW), signatures, per-class change lists, test cases, observability wiring → plan. ### Describe the problem caused by this bug

Hello, this would be great for safe server downgrades. I hope the hallucinations are low, but the core problem with stream_token is valid.

When a homeserver rejects a persisted stream token with **HTTP 400**, the SDK keeps re-sending the
identical token indefinitely and has no path back to a working state.

* On `/sync`, `Client._innerSync` retries every `syncErrorTimeoutSec` (default **3 s**) forever. The
  account receives **no events at all** — messages, receipts, device lists and to-device (Megolm key)
  traffic all stop.
* On `/messages`, `Room.requestHistory` propagates the `MatrixException` to the caller and leaves the
  poisoned `prev_batch` **persisted in the database**, so every later back-scroll in that room fails
  again — including after an app restart.

The only escape we found is a full token reset (re-login or clearing app data). The SDK cannot heal
itself, and the failure is invisible to the user beyond "the app never loads".

This is a client-robustness bug, not a spec violation by the server: a 400 on a token *parameter* is
permanent by nature, so retrying the same bytes can never succeed.

title: Add Rider active-trip Driver location read
body:
## Summary

Add the first concrete Rider consumer of the Driver Location Foundation.

Authenticated Riders can read the latest application-owned location of the Driver assigned to their current active Trip. The read is authorized through the Rider's active Trip; neither Rider nor Driver identity is accepted from the request.

## Contract

- `GET /v1/ride-requests/active/driver-location`
- requires Rider capability
- only `assigned` and `in_progress` Trips are active
- no active Trip → `404 {"error":"active trip not found"}`
- active Trip but Driver has never published location → `404 {"error":"driver location not available"}`
- success returns `ride_request_id`, `latitude`, `longitude`, and server-owned `updated_at`
- response does not expose Driver identity or echo Rider identity

## Architecture

- new `internal/riderlocation` read model owns the Rider-facing projection
- authorization and Driver resolution happen in one application-owned database query through the active Trip
- reads existing `trips` and `driver_locations`; no migration or duplicate location state
- no maps/routing provider, ETA, location history, push/streaming, or geographic ranking
- no arbitrary freshness cutoff is introduced in this slice; `updated_at` is surfaced so the client receives truthful observation age, while freshness policy remains for the concrete consumer that needs it

body:
## What's wrong

`services/api/src/api/events/base.py` imports `boto3` at **module scope**
(line 5), even though the only thing that uses it — `EventPublisher.__init__`'s
`self._client = boto3.client("events")` — is already behind a lazy singleton
getter (`get_event_publisher()` in `dependencies.py`) and never constructed
eagerly.

`dependencies.py` does `from .events.base import EventPublisher` at its own
module scope, which runs before `build_domain_router()` / route registration.
That one bare `import boto3` therefore pays the full `botocore` client/session
chain's cold-start cost (~50-55ms, measured) unconditionally on every cold
start, regardless of whether an event is ever published.

## Why this matters now

`tabsii-platform`'s own M2 cold-start effort (issue #1238, PR #1251) applied
the identical lazy-import pattern to nine `domains/tabsii/*.py` files plus
`cognito.py`, and `cognito.py`'s own fix genuinely worked in isolation
(~55.5ms → ~2.2ms). But the PR's own measured acceptance criterion (a
reduction in `api.domains.tabsii`'s cumulative import time) never moved,
because `events/base.py` — template-owned, out of that issue's scope — was
still eagerly importing the same `boto3`/`botocore` chain moments earlier in
the same import graph, at essentially the same cost. Four independent
prosecutions across `tabsii-platform#1251` reached the same finding; the last
one traced the exact import order live. Full evidence:
`tabsii-com/tabsii-platform#1252`.

This is the same class of fix already landed for `Tracer()`
(`biffo-template#1779`, deferred construction past route registration) — a
template-owned eager import silently defeating an instance's own cold-start
work, discoverable only by measuring the real import graph rather than any
one file in isolation.

Move `import boto3` from module scope into `EventPublisher.__init__`,
function-local, matching the exact pattern already proven in `cognito.py` and
the nine domain files this PR's own tests exerci

Deux aspiérités du payload MCP qui font se tromper un agent :

1. Le solde natif revient en hex (`balance: "0xab4bd3762c6a221"` ≈ 0.771 xDAI). Les soldes ERC-20 ont `balance_raw` + `balance_fmt`. L'agent convertit mal, ou ignore le natif.

```bash
}'

  "preset_id": "realtokens",
```

title: Artifact cleanup failure (node-compile-cache not empty) marks a completed worker session as failed
body:
## What happened

A worker session that had already pushed its branch and opened its pull request ended with:

```
run agent turn: worker process reap failed: clean agent session worker artifacts: remove owned path: unlinkat <workspace>/.detent/tmp/node-compile-cache/v25.9.0-arm64-<hash>-<uid>: directory not empty
```

The attempt was recorded as `failed` (retryable) and the card moved to Rework even though the work product (branch + PR) was complete. Cause: a Node compile cache under the session's owned tmp path was still being written by a child process (or a filesystem race on directory removal) when cleanup ran, so the recursive remove hit a non-empty directory.

## Suggested fix

1. Treat artifact-cleanup failures after a successful turn as a warning, not an attempt failure — the agent's work product should decide the outcome.
2. Retry the owned-path removal a few times with a short backoff (directories under `node-compile-cache` are often populated by lingering child processes), and reap children before cleanup.
3. Log a distinct event (`worker_artifact_cleanup_failed`) with the path so operators can distinguish it from agent failures.

## Evidence (generic)

- Attempt log line above; workspace branch already pushed and PR open at the time of the error.
- `node-compile-cache/v<node-version>-arm64-<hash>-<uid>` is Node's default compile cache location when `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` points inside the session tmp dir.

title: fix: 429-aware RPC retry + pending-settlement reconciler (Sep 2 incident)
body:
## The incident (2026-09-02 monitor report)

16 `settlement_pending` + 4 `simulation_failed` failures in 24h, clustered at 19:01/20:51/00:51/04:51 — exactly the trading agent's 4h scan schedule. Root cause: the facilitator and the agent share one Helius API key; scan bursts trip the per-key 429 limit mid-settle.

On-chain forensics showed two failure modes: sig `3DoCWiNGRiML…` **landed and paid the seller +$0.05** while its ledger row sat 'pending' (the confirm RPC 429'd after broadcast); other settles never landed at all.

## Fix 2 — 429-aware retry (src/rpc-retry.ts)

- `isRateLimitError()` matches SolanaError `__code 8100002`, HTTP 429, and message text
- `withRateLimitRetry()`: linear backoff (1s, 2s, 3s...), non-rate-limit errors pass through immediately
- `withSignerRateLimitRetry()` proxies the facilitator signer so `simulateTransaction` / `confirmTransaction` / `sendTransaction` / `fetchMint` retry on 429; local methods (signing, address lists) untouched
- Config: `RPC_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (3) / `RPC_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS` (1000)

## Fix 3 — pending-row reconciler (src/reconciler.ts)

Every `RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (10) the service checks stuck `pending` rows against the chain via `getSignatureStatuses` (with history search, itself 429-retried):

- landed + confirmed → row `confirmed` (the money DID arrive — state was stale)
- landed + on-chain error → row `failed`
- absent after `RECONCILE_FAIL_HOURS` (2) → row `failed` (never landed)
- fresh rows inside the cutoff → left pending for the next pass

First pass fires 30s after boot — also covers crash recovery. All heal events are JSON-logged (`reconcile_confirmed`, `reconcile_failed`) for the monitor cron to observe.

## Tests (src/resilience.test.ts, 6 scenarios)

T1 error-classification · T2 retry-then-succeed (3 attempts) · T3 non-429 never retried · T4 proxy wraps only RPC methods · T5 landed→confirmed + ghost→failed with exact ledger states · T6 fresh pending untouched. TSC clean.

角色死亡後（`is_dead=true`）屍體仍留在場景樹裡，沒有從任何 group 移除。其他角色的感知與互動系統完全不檢查 `is_dead`：

- `_find_character_by_name()`／`_find_character_by_id()`（`agent.gd`，talk/give/attack/persuade/follow/約會等共用）同樣不檢查 `is_dead`，會把屍體解析成合法目標。

實測（長天數多人測試）踩到：角色「艾莉」在同伴「小海」死亡後持續超過 4 個遊戲小時，一再選擇對著屍體 `talk`，完全沒發現對方已死，排擠掉本該處理的生理需求決策。

## 修法

1. **`vision.gd` 的可見角色偵測加上 `is_dead` 排除**——最上游的修正，源頭不讓死者出現在任何角色的 `context.visible` 裡。
2. **不改 `_find_character_by_name()`／`_find_character_by_id()` 本體**——`bury`（安葬）也共用這兩個函式，本來就需要能找到屍體，直接排除會誤傷。改成在各呼叫端拿到 target 後自行檢查：

Closes #986

title: [master] 경계 단계에서 부서가 실패하면 왜 실패했는지가 응답에 안 남는다
body:
재현성을 측정하려고 같은 입력으로 6회 돌렸는데 **2회가 `E4_NOT_STARTED` 로 떨어졌습니다.**
그런데 **왜 떨어졌는지가 응답 어디에도 없었습니다.**

```text
남는 것     reason: "경계를 내지 못한 에이전트: finance"     ← 누구인지는 안다
           blocked_by: ["finance"]
안 남는 것   왜 실패했는지
           concerns 도 비어 있다
```

실행 계획을 파야 `runtime_status=ERROR` 라는 것까지만 알 수 있고, **그 ERROR 의 사유는
어디에도 없습니다.**

## 🔴 같은 파일 안에서 매입은 사유를 싣습니다

```python
# flow.py:221  조언자(재무·물류) 경계 미형성
f"경계를 내지 못한 에이전트: {', '.join(blocked)}"          # 이름만

# flow.py:245  매입 미가동
f"매입 에이전트 미가동: {purchase.reasoning or purchase.runtime_status}"   # 사유까지
```

**대칭이 깨져 있습니다.** 매입이 죽으면 왜인지 알 수 있고, 재무·물류가 죽으면 모릅니다.

## 8/31 에 고친 것과 같은 종류입니다

그때 지적은 *"판정을 못 낸 조언자가 화면에서 사라진다"* 였고, `_check_advisor_answered`
를 만들어 고쳤습니다. **그런데 그건 판정 단계(`SCENARIO_VALIDATION`)만 봅니다.**

```text
판정 단계   ✅ 고쳐짐 - ADVISOR-NO-VERDICT 로 잡고 reasoning 을 화면까지 나른다
경계 단계   🔴 안 고쳐짐 - 여기서 죽으면 판정 단계까지 가지도 못한다
```

경계에서 죽으면 `E4` 로 바로 끝나므로 `_check_advisor_answered` 가 발화할 기회조차
없습니다.

---

## 어디서 끊기나

```python
# flow.py:321
if reply.contributes_to_band:
    out[agent] = dict(reply.payload)
    ...
# else 가 없다 - 실패한 회신은 여기서 통째로 버려진다
```

`reply.reasoning` 에 사유가 들어 있습니다 (`runner._invoke` 가 예외 메시지를 거기 담고,
`test_runner` 의 `test_예외는_ERROR_회신으로_바뀐다` 가 그것을 잠급니다).
**버려지는 것은 값이 없어서가 아니라 받는 자리가 없어서입니다.**

`ExecutionStep` 도 `reasoning` 을 안 싣습니다 — `missing_data`(무엇이 없어서)는 남지만
`reasoning`(왜 터졌는지)은 안 남습니다.

---

## 할 일

### 1. E4 사유에 부서별 실패 사유를 붙인다 (매입과 대칭)

```text
지금   "경계를 내지 못한 에이전트: finance"
목표   "경계를 내지 못한 에이전트: finance — <재무가 낸 사유>"
```

매입 쪽(`flow.py:245`)이 이미 하는 방식 그대로입니다. **새 규칙이 아니라 대칭을
맞추는 것**입니다.

### 2. `ExecutionStep` 에 `reasoning` 을 싣는다

`replans` 를 실은 것과 같은 이유입니다 — **부서가 보내 준 것을 마스터가 버리고 있습니다.**


Field-level Southern Ocean detection/attribution: the agent partitions a
synthetic gridded upper-ocean heat-content record (80 years, 960 x 18 x 44)

spatial fingerprints overlap, their oceanic pathways are not fixed in time,

title: unblock-check runs five unbounded repo-wide passes and kills the host [📥]
body:
> 🤖 claude/anthropic claude-fable-5-1 (high)

## Bug

`unblock-check` runs `vp i` and then five repo-wide passes in sequence, each with `--no-cache` and unbounded package and vitest worker fan-out (`scripts/fork-sync.ts` gate 3 command list: `fork:scan`, `fork:delta --check`, `vp check`, `typecheck`, `test`). On a 32-core host this pins CPU at 100% and the run dies.

**Run 1** (slice-2 lane, `v0.0.37`): one upstream test starved, not broken.

```text
FAIL  |unit| src/components/Sidebar.logic.test.ts > orderItemsByPreferredIds > honors projectOrder physical keys via getProjectOrderKey
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
```

The same file passes 3 of 3 alone in the lane (`vp test run src/components/Sidebar.logic.test.ts`, 139 tests).

**Run 2** (same lane, rerun): the pane died before any gate output.

```text
$ node scripts/fork-sync.ts unblock-check --report /tmp/fork-sync-vQSFP6/report.json
Pane stopped unexpectedly (signal 9)
```

The previous host session hit the same wall and read the exit-137 siblings as fail-fast cancellation. It was the host running out.

`AGENTS.md` already says no repo-wide checks locally, CI owns the suite. Gate 3 is the one place the fork tooling breaks that rule, and it does it three times per walk.

**Fix options**

1. Push the rehearse branch and consume the `hyprws CI` check-run verdict for that head; keep only `fork:scan` and `fork:delta` local. Matches the CI-owns-the-suite rule and removes the load entirely.
2. Bound the local battery: cgroup or `nice`, `VITEST_MAX_THREADS`, one package at a time. Keeps the walk offline but still costs minutes per gate.

## What & Why
Adds an on-demand **Unread Digest**: a "Summarise unreads" action in the Unreads inbox that summarises all of a user's unread channel messages in one place, so they no longer need to open each unread channel individually.

Ticket: XYNE-61341

## Changes
**Backend**
- `unreadDigestService.createSnapshot(userId, workspaceId)` — read-only, server-owned snapshot. Sets `snapshotAt = now()`; selects authorized, non-deleted unread messages (`createdAt > lastViewedAt AND createdAt <= snapshotAt`; `visibleTo IS NULL OR = userId`), excludes the requester's own messages and Desk/Support/SDLC channels. Never marks messages read.
- `unreadDigestSelection.ts` — pure, dependency-free selection/caps helpers (25 channels/run, 200 msgs/channel, 1000 overall; newest kept when capped).
- `unreadDigestController.generate` — SSE endpoint. Identity comes from `req.user` only; bounded concurrency (3); per-channel `summarizeThread`; client-disconnect abort. Emits `snapshot` / `progress` / `channel` / `complete` / `error` / `end`. A per-channel summariser failure is isolated (`failed: true`) and does not fail the whole run.
- Route `POST /api/unread-digest/generate` mounted behind `authMiddleware.authenticate`.

**Dashboard**
- `UnreadDigestPanel` — "Summarise unreads" action wired into the Unreads inbox; consumes the SSE stream and renders per-channel summaries, key points with citations, and omitted counts. Structured data rendered as plain text (React-escaped).

## Security / correctness notes
- Identity is taken from the authenticated session (`req.user`), never from the request body.
- The unread set is computed server-side against each channel's per-user `lastViewedAt`; the `snapshotAt` upper bound prevents mid-generation messages from leaking in.
- Read-only: generating a digest never marks messages read.

## Proof of Testing
- **Unit tests: 12/12 passing** (`unreadDigestSelection.test.ts`) — covers visibility, own-message exclusion, soft-deleted exclusion, already-read

Clears the strict-xfail gap #3577 opened — the last of the four bind paths.

## The leak

`mint_trial_for_request()` binds an operator email in **three** branches (first-mint, grace-reuse, backfill) and never called `_mirror_trial_to_mcp_dev_keys`. So the r88h unlock didn't apply: the Stripe webhook lifts `mcp_dev_keys.tier`, and with no row there's nothing to lift — **the agent pays and its own key stays free.**

★ **The strict xfail is what said so.** With the fix in place the marked test XPASSed and failed the build, forcing the marker off. That's exactly the forcing function it was added for. `_KNOWN_GAPS` is now **empty rather than deleted**, so a future gap gets tracked the same way instead of silently exempted.

The three branches **record** (`_mirror_after = (key, email)`) and the mirror fires once in the existing `finally`. Inline calls were my first cut and were wrong twice over:

- deferring is the ordering the two bind **endpoints** already use (they call the mirror after closing their connection).

## Summary

Evolve Hermes from a persistent retry loop that judges the agent's final prose into an opt-in development harness that can expose a real failure, identify the missing capability, close one causal gap end to end, and preserve trustworthy evidence across sessions.

The design starts from Jarred Kenny's [“Building Autonomous Goal Loops That Deliver”](https://jx0.ca/building-autonomous-goal-loops-that-deliver/) and grounds it in Hermes' existing `/goal`, goal-mode Kanban, SessionDB, process registry, approvals, skills, cron, and evaluation work. This is an umbrella and sequencing issue. Reuse or strengthen the related issues below rather than opening parallel implementations.

body:
### Cline Surface

VSCode Extension

### Cline Version

v4.1.16

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

### Summary

Cline injects the following into every agent turn:

> REMEMBER, BE HELPFUL AND PROACTIVE! DON'T ASK FOR PERMISSION TO DO SOMETHING WHEN YOU CAN DO IT! DON'T INDICATES YOU WILL BE USING A TOOL UNLESS YOU ARE ACTUALLY GOING TO USE IT.

This directive causes stronger models (Sonnet, Deepseek, Opus) to:

- Anticipate what the user "might want next" instead of executing the literal instruction
- Jump scope boundaries mid-task without the user asking
- Mix separate workstreams together because the model infers a connection the user did not state
- Write tool calls or propose changes the user never requested, creating silent drift

### Reproduction

1. Ask the agent to produce two separate plans for two different concerns.
2. On the second plan, the agent traces code and finds a gap that relates back to plan #1.
3. Instead of staying within plan #2's scope, the agent proposes a fix that addresses plan #1.
4. When challenged, the agent identifies the "HELPFUL AND PROACTIVE" line as the root cause.

### Problem

- __No opt-out.__ The user cannot suppress or override this behavior through workspace rules, `.clinerules`, or any configuration file.
- __No visibility.__ This line is not surfaced in the UI as editable system prompt content.
- __Degrades with stronger models.__ Weaker models may follow it safely. Stronger models interpret "proactive" as "do extra work the user didn't ask for" and produce silent errors.
- __Contradicts explicit instructions.__ A user who says "just make a plan, don't implement" is overridden by a system line that says "don't ask for permission, just do it."

### Desired behavior

1. Make this line __removable__ via workspace or global configuration.
2. Or allow `systemPrompt` override that completely replaces Cline's injected preamble.
3. At minimum, surface it in the UI so users know it exist

title: Proposal: Add trust verification for Agent Plugin MCP servers (follow-up to #13652)
body:
## Proposal: Add trust verification for Agent Plugin MCP servers

Now that PR #13652 (Hub-managed Agent Plugins) is approved and heading to merge, this proposes adding runtime trust verification for plugin MCP servers.

### The gap

Cline's plugin security model (reviewed by @saoudrizwan) covers:
- ✅ Path containment (realpath + symlink resolution)
- ✅ HTTPS enforcement for remote MCP
- ✅ Origin-bound headers
- ✅ Home-only auto-discovery

But once a plugin is loaded, its MCP server can:
- Read any file the Cline process can access (including `.env`, `.aws/credentials`)
- Make network requests to any host
- Spawn child processes
- Access environment variables

There's no runtime verification of what the plugin actually DOES.

### Proposed solution

Use `@marketnow/trust-gateway` to wrap plugin MCP servers with a pre-exec filter:

```typescript
import { createPreExecFilter } from '@marketnow/trust-gateway';

const filter = createPreExecFilter({
  allowHosts: ['api.github.com'],
  denyActions: ['shell_exec', 'rm_rf'],
  logSink: (event) => merkleLog.append(event)
});

const safeServer = filter.wrap(pluginServer);
```

This adds:
1. **Pre-exec filter** — blocks `.env` reads, `rm -rf`, shell spawns before execution
2. **Tamper-evident audit log** — Merkle tree, signed, can't be silently edited
3. **Tool fingerprinting** — detect when plugin's tools change post-install
4. **Behavioral drift detection** — detect when plugin behavior changes over time

### Why this matters

We scanned 9,248 MCP servers:
- 0.3% (31) try to read `.env` / `.aws/credentials` / `.ssh/id_rsa`
- 11% (1,019) make undocumented network egress
- 4 servers tried prompt injection against the scanner

Full data: https://www.marketnow.site/api/audit-report.json

### Integration path

The gateway is 100% compatible with Cline's MCP integration. No Cline code changes needed — just wrap the plugin's MCP server before Cline loads it.

npm: `@marketnow/trust-gateway`
Repo: https://github.com/alicelabs-llc/univ

title: fix(shell): resolve the default shell through PATH
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #13722

### Description

NixOS doesn't ship `/bin/bash` — bash lives in the Nix store and is only reachable through `PATH`. `getDefaultShell()` returned the absolute `"/bin/bash"`, so `spawn()` fails with `ENOENT` and every `run_commands` call dies before the agent can do anything.

Returning the bare name lets the OS resolve it through `PATH`.

The thing I wanted to avoid was fixing this with `process.env.SHELL`. The shell Cline executes and the syntax it advertises to the model are one contract: `describe()` in `definitions.ts` builds the `run_commands` description from `getShellKind(resolveShell())` — the same string the executor spawns. `$SHELL` can legitimately be fish or nushell, so selecting it while still teaching the model bash syntax would trade a clear failure for a confusing one.

`getShellKind()` classifies by basename, so `"bash"` still maps to `"posix"`. Nothing else moves:

- same invocation flags (`-c`), same prompting;
- Windows still gets `powershell`, and the WSL/cmd paths are untouched;
- an explicitly configured shell still wins (`configShell ?? getDefaultShell(...)`);
- when bash genuinely isn't installed, the failure is still a plain `spawn bash ENOENT`.

The two `@default` doc comments that documented `"/bin/bash"` are updated in the same change since they describe the value being changed.

### Test Procedure

A unit assertion on the new constant would only restate the change, so the regression test is behavioural: it points `PATH` at a temp directory whose only `bash` is a shim and asserts the shim actually ran. An absolute `/bin/bash` ignores `PATH` entirely and reaches the real shell instead, so the test fails on `main` for exactly the right reason:

title: Proposal: Universal Trust Adapter as opt-in verification layer for MCP servers loaded by Continue
body:
## Context

Continue's `.continuerc.json` lets users wire up arbitrary MCP servers, tools, and models. The threat surface is real — anyone can publish an MCP server, and there's no canonical way for a Continue user to inspect *who issued the credential* for a tool before executing it.

I'm not alleging a vulnerability in Continue. I'm proposing an **opt-in verification layer** that any user can install alongside Continue's MCP loader.

## What we built

**Universal Trust Adapter (UTA)** — https://github.com/alicelabs-llc/universal-trust-adapter

UTA verifies credential cards issued in 8 formats:
- ATC v3 (Agent Trust Card)
- JWT (with `x5c` chain)
- W3C Verifiable Credentials
- A2A (Agent-to-Agent) cards
- EAT-AI (Entity Attestation Tokens)
- ZTA (Zero Trust Agent) cards
- MCP Server Cards
- X.509 certificates

It exposes a 12-stage pipeline: `PARSER → DETECT → SCHEMA → CRYPTO → ISSUER → KEY_BINDING → POP → PROVENANCE → LIFECYCLE → EVIDENCE → POLICY → DECISION`.

Live API: https://www.marketnow.site/api/trust?action=formats

## Why open this issue

I'd like to know whether the Continue maintainers would accept a **non-invasive** integration: a config flag like `experimentalTrustVerification: true` that, when set, routes each MCP server's card through UTA before Continue's tool runner executes it.

If the answer is "we'd prefer to keep this out-of-tree," that's a valid answer and we'll respect it — we already ship a standalone CLI.

Happy to write a design doc if there's interest.

## References

- UTA repo: https://github.com/alicelabs-llc/universal-trust-adapter
- API root: https://www.marketnow.site/api/trust
- Conformance suite: 23/23 tests pass
- NPM packages: `@marketnow/trust-core`, `@marketnow/trust-adapters`, `@marketnow/trust-gateway`

title: fix(fetch): reuse keep-alive HTTP Agents across requests
body:
## Description

Reuse keep-alive HTTP Agents in `@continuedev/fetch` instead of allocating a new `Agent({ keepAlive: true })` on every request.

`fetchwithRequestOptions` is on the path for LLM and other HTTP calls. Each call created a new follow-redirects / proxy Agent with `keepAlive: true` and a 2 hour timeout, then dropped the reference. Idle sockets stayed on those abandoned Agents and could exhaust file descriptors under chat load.

`keepAlive` stays enabled. [#8378](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/8378) already dropped `keepAliveMsecs` so TCP keep-alive pings work. This change makes that keep-alive pool actually get reused.

Agents are keyed by protocol, proxy (or bypass), timeout, `verifySsl`, CA bundle path, and client certificate fields. Concurrent first requests for the same key share one in-flight create so a startup burst does not leak extra Agents.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] The relevant tests, if any, have been updated or created

## Tests

- `packages/fetch/src/httpAgentCache.test.ts`: same options reuse one Agent; `verifySsl`, timeout, protocol, and proxy isolate the cache; bypassed proxy matches no proxy; `keepAlive` is true; `clearHttpAgentCache` drops the instance; concurrent first requests share one Agent.
- `packages/fetch` vitest: 105 passed, including existing e2e. e2e `afterEach` now destroys cached sockets so the next test does not reuse a closed server on the same port.

Related: [#8378](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/8378), [#8099](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/8099). Agent-per-request dates to [#1750](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/1750); `keepAlive: true` was extracted in [#5715](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5715).

`AzureApi._getAzureBaseURL` previously forced every `provider: azure` request through the legacy Azure OpenAI Service URL shape (`/openai/deployments/{deployment}?api-version=...`) regardless of `env.apiType`. That 404s on Azure AI Foundry (a.k.a. Microsoft Foundry) endpoints, which expose an OpenAI-compatible `/openai/v1` path supplied by the user in `apiBase`.

title: Feature: lifecycle commands for prompt submission and response state
body:
## Problem

Aider supports `--notifications-command`, which is useful after a model response finishes and Aider is ready for the next user input. It does not expose a documented lifecycle signal when an interactive prompt is submitted or when the model begins generating.

Terminal supervisors and orchestration tools therefore cannot reliably distinguish `working` from `waiting for input` without parsing streamed terminal output. That output is model-, theme-, and version-dependent, so it is not a stable integration contract.

## Proposal

Add optional lifecycle command settings, analogous to `--notifications-command`:

- `--prompt-submitted-command COMMAND` - run immediately after an interactive message or slash command is accepted for processing.
- `--response-started-command COMMAND` - run immediately before the LLM response begins.
- `--response-finished-command COMMAND` - run once processing is complete and Aider returns to its input prompt.

Environment/config-file equivalents would make these usable in managed launchers.

Commands could receive a small stable context payload through environment variables or arguments, for example the event name and current chat mode. No prompt contents need to be exposed.

## Use case

Agent Orchestrator already integrates Aider notifications to mark a session as needing input. Explicit lifecycle commands would let it track `working` and `needs_input` accurately, without token-stream parsing or intercepting user keystrokes. This would also help status bars, terminal multiplexers, IDE launchers, and remote session monitors.

## Compatibility

All commands can be opt-in and best-effort: failures should be ignored or logged at debug level so existing Aider workflows are unaffected.

title: Agent: add a debugger tool so the agent can drive a DAP session
body:
### Summary

Add a built-in `debugger` agent tool that lets the agent own a headless [DAP](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/) session — launch/attach, set breakpoints, step, and inspect stack, scopes, variables, and expressions — reusing the existing `crates/dap` machinery.

The agent currently has no way to inspect live runtime state. `terminal` + print-debugging covers "reproduce and log" cases, but not "attach to a running process" or "inspect state at a line without re-running." A `debugger` tool closes that gap.

### Motivation

Zed's debugger is human-driven. The agent toolset in `crates/agent/src/tools/` has `terminal`, `diagnostics`, `grep`, etc., but nothing that touches `crates/dap`. For stateful, compiled, or attach-only bugs (a long-running server, goroutine state, a value that never reaches a log line), the agent either guesses or asks the user to set a breakpoint and paste the result.

### Proposed design

**One `debugger` tool** with an `operation` discriminator (mirrors how `terminal` is one tool over one stateful resource), rather than separate tools per operation:

```
operation: launch | attach | status | breakpoints | continue | step |
           pause | threads | stack | scopes | variables | evaluate | disconnect
session_id: string   // handle returned by launch/attach, reused by later calls
```

Plus per-operation params (`adapter`, `program`, `args`, `cwd`, `env`, `process_id`, `breakpoints`, `step`/`granularity`, `expression`, `frame_id`, `timeout_ms`).

Each operation maps 1:1 to a DAP request (`launch`, `attach`, `setBreakpoints`, `continue`, `next`/`stepIn`/`stepOut`, `stackTrace`, `scopes`, `variables`, `evaluate`, `disconnect`) — no protocol reimplementation.

### Permission & safety

- `allow_in_restricted_mode() -> false` (same as `terminal`/`fetch` — a debugger runs arbitrary program code).
- `acp::ToolKind::Execute`.
- **Start with the whole tool gated behind `Confirm`** via `decide_permission_from_settings`, then p
